title: Mapping-space excision for a simplicial indexing pushout
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor categories and right-pinched mapping spaces as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with all objects small in a sufficiently large fixed universe. Let $i:A\to D$ and $j:A\to B$ be maps of simplicial sets, with $i$ degreewise injective (each $i_n:A_n\to D_n$ is injective), and put $K=B\amalg_A D$. For any quasicategory $\mathcal C$ and any two diagrams $F,G:K\to\mathcal C$, restriction induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(F,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)}(F|_B,G|_B)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)}(F|_A,G|_A)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal C)}(F|_D,G|_D).$$
Here, for maps $u:U\to W$ and $v:V\to W$ of Kan complexes, $U\times_W^h V$ is the space of triples $(a,b,\gamma)$, where $a\in U$, $b\in V$, and $\gamma$ is a path in $W$ from $u(a)$ to $v(b)$, with all higher simplices of these data; a model is $U\times_{W,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,W)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,W}V$. The comparison sends a transformation to its two restrictions and the constant path between their identical restrictions to $A$. It is natural in both diagrams and compatible, up to coherent homotopy, with precomposition and postcomposition of transformations. No existence of limits or colimits in $\mathcal C$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated mapping-space consequence of Kerodon Example 4.5.5.12 (indexing pushout along a monomorphism), Proposition 4.5.5.4 (0340, functor-category categorical pullback), Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3, restriction is an isofibration), Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8) and Remark 4.6.1.23 (01P9, ordinary morphism-space Kan fibrations and homotopy fibers), and Propositions 4.6.5.5 (01L0) and 4.6.5.10 (01L5, pinched spaces are Kan and their natural pinch inclusions are homotopy equivalences). Read online 2026-10-16; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $Q_S=\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal C)$ for $S=A,B,D,K$. They are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory]. There is a strict isomorphism of simplicial sets $Q_K=Q_B\times_{Q_A}Q_D$. Indeed an $n$-simplex is a map $K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$. Degree by degree, product with the set $(\Delta^n)_m$ preserves pushouts of sets, so $K\times\Delta^n=(B\times\Delta^n)\amalg_{A\times\Delta^n}(D\times\Delta^n)$. A map out is exactly a pair agreeing on $A\times\Delta^n$, and this description commutes with every face and degeneracy. The formula for $Q_S$ is the one in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. No injectivity of $j$ is used.

source.place: Prism-independent degreewise pushout calculation; functor closure from the cited calculus node.

proof.text: Restriction $Q_D\to Q_A$ is an isofibration, hence an inner fibration, by the restriction clause of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], because $i$ is degreewise injective. Put $H_S=U_{Q_S}(F|_S,G|_S)$ using that node's displayed endpoint-fiber definition. By the internal-hom formula in Step 1, an $n$-simplex of $H_S$ is a map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to Q_S$ constant at $F|_S$ and $G|_S$ on the two endpoint faces. Swapping the product factors identifies it with a prism $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to Q_S$; this identification commutes with restriction in $\Delta^n$ and with postcomposition. The final clause of the cited node, applied to $Q_D\to Q_A$, gives a Kan fibration $H_D\to H_A$ between Kan complexes. Applied to the identity inner fibration of each $Q_S$, the same clause makes every $H_S$ Kan. All quasicategory hypotheses hold by Step 1. There is no fibration requirement on $Q_B\to Q_A$.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3) and Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8); elementary expansion of the endpoint fiber by the internal-hom definition.

proof.text: The strict pullback in Step 1 gives a strict isomorphism $H_K=H_B\times_{H_A}H_D$. An $n$-simplex on either side is a pair of maps $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to Q_B,Q_D$ agreeing in $Q_A$, with their two endpoint faces constant at the restrictions of $F,G$. The pullback property glues them uniquely into $Q_K$; the endpoint conditions glue to the constant $F,G$ endpoint conditions. Taking faces or degeneracies before or after gluing gives the same map. This proves the isomorphism of entire simplicial sets, rather than of their sets of components.

source.place: Elementary prism calculation using the definition in Step 2 and the strict pullback in Step 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to $H_B\to H_A\leftarrow H_D$. Step 2 verifies that all three are Kan and the second leg is a Kan fibration. Combining it with Step 3 gives a weak homotopy equivalence $r_H:H_K\to H_B\times^h_{H_A}H_D$. The map is the pair of restrictions together with the constant path at their common restriction, exactly as specified by the cited comparison.

Put $M_S=\operatorname{Map}_{Q_S}(F|_S,G|_S)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], both $M_S$ and $H_S$ are Kan and the specified pinch maps $\iota_S:M_S\to H_S$ are weak homotopy equivalences. In the prism notation of Step 2 they send $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to Q_S$ to $\sigma c_n$, where $c_n(k,0)=k$ and $c_n(k,1)=n+1$. For a restriction functor $q$, the equality $q(\sigma c_n)=(q\sigma)c_n$ proves strict commutation with restriction in every degree. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to these maps for $S=B,A,D$; the required squares commute by this equality and all six complexes are Kan. The resulting map $\iota_P:M_B\times^h_{M_A}M_D\to H_B\times^h_{H_A}H_D$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. For the map $r_M$ asserted in the item, $\iota_P r_M=r_H\iota_K$ strictly: on each simplex both sides give the two restricted prism maps and the constant path at their common restriction. The right side is a weak equivalence by Step 4 and the pinch comparison. Therefore $r_M$ is a weak homotopy equivalence: on components its map is the composite of the inverse bijection induced by $\iota_P$ with the bijection induced by $r_H\iota_K$, and on each based homotopy group the identical cancellation of two isomorphisms applies. This uses only the definition of weak homotopy equivalence from Step 1.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 4.6.5.10 and Proposition 3.4.0.9: comparison of the two mapping-space models.

proof.text: The equivalence just established is the specified restriction and constant-path map. To check its naturality and composition coherence directly, let $T$ be any simplicial set and $h:K\times T\to\mathcal C$ any family of diagram data. For every $\alpha:T'\to T$ and $S=A,B,D$, restriction satisfies $(h\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times\alpha))|_{S\times T'}=(h|_{S\times T})\circ(\mathrm{id}_S\times\alpha)$. Also restriction from $B$ or $D$ to $A$ gives the identical map $h|_{A\times T}$. Taking $T=\Delta^2$ shows that a triangle witnessing a composite restricts to the same composite triangle on each shape; arbitrary $T=\Delta^r$ and all their face and degeneracy maps give all higher coherence witnesses, including those for precomposition and postcomposition as the endpoints vary. Inserting the constant path is induced by $T\times\Delta^1\to T$, and this projection commutes with every $\alpha$. Hence the constant-path data commute with these same triangle and higher-simplex restrictions. This proves naturality in both diagrams and compatibility with precomposition, postcomposition and their coherent homotopies, without choosing inverse pinch maps. Only products and pushouts of indexing simplicial sets were used; no limits or colimits in $\mathcal C$ were required.
